newsitem.title: USA: First Team sees lower Q2 sales, profit.
newsitem.headline: First Team sees lower Q2 sales, profit.

text.p: First Team Sports Inc, which makes in-line roller skates, said Wednesday that it expects earnings for the second quarter to be between $0.03 and $0.07 a share, "significantly lower" than analysts' estimates.
Net sales for the quarter, ending August 31, are expected to be in a range of $15 and $16 million.
In the year-ago second quarter, First Team posted net sales of $23.2 million and earnings of $0.32 a share.
First Team blamed the current retail climate and competitive pricing for the impact on its near-term results.
First Team did not specify the current range of analysts' estimates for second quarter earnings. But First Call shows a mean estimate for the quarter of $0.29 and a range of $0.17 to $0.39.

"Because of the overall retail slowdown in sporting goods purchases and continued excess inventories in the marketplace, our revenues, margins, and earnings will be significantly lower than expected," John Egart, president, said in a statement. "We believe this excess inventory situation will not correct itself until the Christmas season, which will likely affect third quarter results."
He added that First Team has been aggressively "cleaning out" excess inventories in the second quarter. Combined with third quarter bookings, this is expected to result in a stronger fourth quarter.

"On the positive side, UltraWheels brand products have sold very well throughout the spring and summer, but due to the limited 'open-to-buy' opportunities by major retailers, we have been unable to fully capitalize on our recent product introductions," Egart said.
International sales continue to expand and will account for about 32 percent of First Team's second quarter revenues, he said.

"Our new line of products, introduced at recent trade shows in Chicago and Munich, have been received extremely well, especially our Sabotage line of aggressive skates and our new soft boot line," Egart said. "In fact, already we have received increased item listings with many major retailers for spring."
